title: Private Server Implementation Eligibility
scope: This file assesses which private-server features are ELIGIBLE for implementation in the next phase (G20), based on the confirmed three-part contract test (client request + server response + state advancement).
eligibility_criteria: A feature is ELIGIBLE only when all three hold from game-side evidence: (1) confirmed client request contract, (2) required server response contract, (3) state advancement/completion behavior.

features.caveat: OpenKey validation, master-data load, and version handshake endpoints exist (resource.py, game_data.py, version.py) but are not confirmed against the game's exact HTTP payload contracts. Proceed only with captures or client-observed evidence.
features.g20_scope: Validate existing HTTP startup routes against observed game behavior.

features.caveat: Card flow runs through the NESYS named pipe (\\.\pipe\nesys_games). Whether the game is pipe server or client, and the exact pipe message format, is UNRESOLVED. Full external-registration context also missing.
features.g20_scope: Resolve pipe role (server vs client) via control-flow; only then build a minimal local adapter.

contract_status.client_request: PARTIAL (HTTP server bind + TCP entry/cancel strings)

features.caveat: matching.py and tcp_server.py exist but their message IDs and payloads are built from synthetic/protocol evidence, NOT confirmed game-side. EntryMatching/CancelMatching/ReMatching strings confirm intent, not the exact TCP frames.
features.g20_scope: Capture real TCP matching exchanges to confirm request/response/state before finalizing.

features.caveat: Battle commands (EntryBurst, ChangeBurstMode, CancelBurst, BurstUpdate, BurstRejectPlayer, BurstSelect) are strings only; payload proto definitions not verified from the client. Battle requires the TCP exchange to be observed.
features.g20_scope: Defer until TCP matching/battle exchange evidence obtained.

features.caveat: HTTP endpoints exist but no confirmed request/response contract or duplication behavior from the game side.
features.g20_scope: Confirm HTTP result-handling contract; add idempotency based on evidence.

contract_status.client_request: PARTIAL (BindHttpErrorCallback, RequestNesysReconnect, 'Disconnect GameServer. Try to Reconnect!')

features.caveat: Error callback and reconnection intent confirmed by strings, but exact behavior contract is not.
features.g20_scope: Confirm error semantics; align synthetic error handler to evidence.

features.caveat: Production certificate provisioning at https://cert2.nesys.jp and GALAXYIO card trust flow are EXCLUDED from the private server (production trust dependency, not operator-controlled).

architecture_recommendation.detail: Two-tier service: (1) a proxy/adapter that keeps the game's existing endpoint expectations (hosts-file/DNS redirect) while routing HTTP/ TCP traffic to the Python server, and (2) the existing Python HTTP+TCP server with confirmed contracts. Local NESYS pipe adapter added only after pipe-role resolution.
rationale: The game has NO supported endpoint override; operator-level redirect (hosts file) is the only practical path
Multi-transport reality (HTTP + TCP + local pipe) requires a composite surface
Cleanroom synthetic foundation remains intact; production adapter is gated on evidence
Matches the existing deployed architecture (HTTP :4001, proxy :80, TCP :6666)
explicitly_rejected: Option D (monolithic single-port) — incompatible with multi-transport game client evidence
Running the proxy on a non-80 port — the game's hardcoded URL uses default HTTP port 80
Any modification/redirection of the game executables (integrity constraint)

analysis_method: Assess game-side evidence (static PE analysis) against the three-part contract test
notes: Matching, battle, and result are NOT fully eligible without confirmed client request + server response + state advancement from captures
Local adapter justified ONLY where game demonstrably requires local IPC
NESYS card trust flow is excluded, not merely deferred, because it is a production trust dependency
